$comment: The languages Cubeulator is translated into: the one list the language manager, the catalogue generator and the translation tests all read.
code: what is stored under the settings key language/code. file: the catalogue's name, cubeulator_<file>.ts. tag: the locale (QLocale name) numbers and dates follow while the language is chosen.
name: the language written in itself. Never translated and never in strings.json: it is data, so that the list is readable by someone who cannot read the interface.
plurals: how many forms Qt's rule for the language has (measured with lconvert, not recalled); a plural string carries exactly that many forms.
rtl: the language is written right to left. The manager checks it against QLocale and a test fails if they disagree.

translated: false until the language has been through E5. A language that is not translated still ships: every string falls back to the English. The translation tests require a language marked true to have no unfinished entry.

draft: true when the catalogue is a complete first translation that no fluent reader has been through yet (machine-assisted). It is installed and shown like any finished entry, so the language works; `translated` stays false until a reader has reviewed it. Nothing requires a draft to stay complete: a string added later falls back to the English until it is translated. strings_to_ts.py --status says which languages are drafts.
The pseudo-locale is never in the list a person chooses from; it is reached through CUBEULATOR_LOCALE=xx only.
